answer: Joint-liability cohorts resist Sybils: new identities are dealt at random into small cohorts sharing one pooled bond, so one proven fake forfeits the whole cohort's stake, like a gale stripping an orchard bare when one bad tree is found. Members therefore audit each other, and a farmer wanting ten thousand fakes must either corrupt whole cohorts or watch opal-clear bonds burn in batches, turning silent duplication into mutual policing. The limit is fairness: one fraudster can punish honest cohort-mates, so cohorts must stay small, rotate often, and allow appeal before slashing.
